verdict.rationale: Lithic documents an official MCP server that can execute live API requests from AI editors. Its own agentic-payments material shows an agent creating virtual cards and configuring Authorization Rules for merchant categories, transaction limits and velocity, and the docs cover card creation, spend limits and program/account/card-level rules. However, scoped or restricted credentials for agents are not evidenced at all, and reading balances and transactions or updating existing cards are not explicitly documented. missing for 10: scoped/least-privilege API keys for agent access, explicit evidence of reading balances and transactions, card update endpoints, independent hands-on corroboration of agent operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can operate my card program — read balances and transactions, create and update cards, and adjust spend controls through the API or an MCP surface with scoped credentials

citations.quote: your AI assistant can search Lithic documentation, inspect endpoint schemas, generate integration code, and execute live API requests, all from within your editor
